thread:
ashley: quick sync — we've seen ~0.4% of sampled traces drop the billing_key when pre-enrich sampling is applied at the edge. noticed on canary traffic, looks correlated with RT=short and packet loss.

sam: ugh. do you mean the key is missing in the envelope after sampling or it never made it into the envelope?

ashley: it arrives at the edge (so upstream SDKs set it), but after pre-enrich sampling the envelope we persist downstream sometimes lacks billing_key. suspect race in the sampling path where envelope is compacted before enrichment rehydrate.

raj: possible causes: compacted envelope dedupe, async fanout reordering, or our sidecar dropping optional keys to save bandwidth. we should enumerate tradeoffs.

kevin: +1 on ordering. if sampler returns quickly and we do a lightweight envelope without enrichments, we might not copy optional headers. two options: 1) ensure billing_key is in the minimal envelope schema (always), 2) add a fallthrough lookup at ingestion that maps trace_id -> billing_key via a short-lived cache/lookup.

ashley: option 1 increases envelope size at the edge for many traces (cost hit across mobile and IoT). option 2 adds extra lookup cost and complexity in ingest, and may not be available in air-gapped/private installs.

sam: can we do a hybrid? put a cheap 64-bit billing fingerprint in the compact envelope, and only do full lookup when fingerprint mismatch or missing? cheaper on wire, still allows fallbacks.

raj: fingerprint approach is neat but we need canonicalization. fingerprints must be stable across SDKs and versions. also need to reason about collision rates and billing attribution errors (false positives/negatives).

kevin: collision math: 64-bit gives ~1e-19 chance per pair; per-day across traces still acceptable if we surface a tolerance threshold and reconciliation. but we need audit logs when we attribute via lookup vs direct key.

ashley: operational concerns: 1) rollout complexity (SDK change + sampler change + ingest gate). 2) retention/TTL for lookup store (how long do we persist mapping?). 3) cost of lookups under spike.

sam: proposed rollout plan: write RFC add `envelope.billing_fp` field (64-bit hex) to minimal envelope, SDKs ship opt-in for 1 release, edge sampler starts emitting fp. ingest has non-blocking ephemeral lookup (memcached tier) to resolve billing_key if missing. if lookup fails, route to fallback model for attribution and mark trace for later backfill.

raj: two cautions: a) private/on-prem customers might not allow memcache; plan must support an opt-out mode with stricter sampling or fallbacks. b) metric implications — attribution changes will affect cost dashboards; need versioned attribution tags so we can compare pre/post.

kevin: implement telemetry tags: `billing.attribution.v` and `billing.attribution.source` (direct|lookup|unknown). console team can then filter/regress. also add an eval that compares key loss rate pre/post.

ashley: decision checklist before RFC: - endpoint schema change (envelope.billing_fp) - SDK compatibility matrix - ingest lookup design and TTL (default: 30m) - opt-out private install flow - telemetry: attribution tags + backfill marker - perf budget for lookups (p95 goal)

sam: I'll draft a short RFC with those bullets and a small PoC to measure envelope size delta and lookup QPS. tagging @raj @kevin for review.

obs-bot: metric alert auto:trace.loss_rate.billing_key > 0.2% for last 1h on canary — created ticket OBS-4321

ashley: thanks — will attach recent traces to OBS-4321 and add initial sample set to the RFC.

kevin: sounds good. one more ask: add a fallback policy in rollout plan that says if lookup latency > 30ms we bypass lookup and mark attribution unknown to avoid inflating tail latency.

ashley: noted. that's in the checklist. will post RFC draft by EOD tomorrow.
